chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdillah ibn Sinan and Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman whose husband has died, whether she observes her waiting period (iddah) in her own house or wherever she wishes. He said: 'Rather, wherever she wishes.' Indeed, when 'Umar died, Ali (peace be upon him) came to Umm Kulthum and took her to his house.
ai.seo_question: Where should a widow observe her waiting period (iddah) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies that a widow's waiting period (iddah) does not mandate confinement to her marital home, granting her the freedom to reside elsewhere. Imam al-Sadiq (a) substantiates this ruling by citing the precedent of Imam Ali (a) taking Umm Kulthum bint Ali to his own residence following the death of Umar, illustrating the practical application of this flexibility within the Ahl al-Bayt's household.
